items.title: Teaching AI to Tell Us Nobody Is Home
items.description: HybridHorizons (previously flagged by Femke as 'genuinely transformative') uses a stats-course example to frame what AI can't detect — a ready classroom device for teaching students the epistemic limits of AI.

items.title: The Mathematicians Are the AI Higher Ed Canary (and Did They Just Find Out They're Humanists?)
items.description: Twenty-five Fields Medalists signing a public letter on AI optimisation is a rare institutional dissent event — directly relevant for framing UU's strategic position on AI and for Femke's boardroom conversations with the rector.

items.title: ChatGPT in Education: Balancing Professional Autonomy, Transforming Relationships and Rethinking the Purpose of Education
items.description: Title maps exactly to Femke's three central questions: what changes for teachers, how power/relationships shift, and what the university is for — likely a strong empirical anchor for the programme plan. Best pick from this week's EJED batch.

items.title: "The Wind Beneath Their Wings": TPACK, Growth Mindset, Commitment, and Teachers' Motivation to Integrate Artificial Intelligence of Things
items.description: Identifies the psychological and pedagogical factors that predict whether teachers actually adopt AI — directly useful for Femke's change-management work with REBO faculty.

items.title: Agentivism: a learning theory for the age of artificial intelligence
items.description: Yan & Gašević propose a new learning theory centred on AI agency — conceptually important for grounding UU's pedagogical framework; connects directly to existing Zettel notes on scaffolding, cognitive load, and what learning actually requires.

items.title: Building AI companions that prioritise learning over performance
items.description: Khosravi, Gašević et al. address the core design tension Femke keeps returning to — AI systems that build genuine competence rather than just producing output — actionable for course design guidance and for WP3.

items.title: Reconceptualizing digital literacy in the AI era: A systematic review of validated frameworks from an ecological perspective
items.description: Systematic review of validated AI-literacy frameworks — directly useful for the literacy component of WP3 and for benchmarking UU's approach against the field.

items.title: ChatGPT for Interdisciplinary Learning: Does it Equally Benefit STEM and Non-STEM Students
items.description: Empirical data on differential ChatGPT benefits across disciplines — directly relevant to REBO (law, economics, governance = non-STEM) and Femke's argument that AI integration must be discipline-sensitive.

items.title: Boy, Was I Wrong About Alpha School
items.description: A first-hand reversal on Alpha School — once cited as an AI-in-education flagship, now described as 'nuclear-waste-level toxic' — useful cautionary case study for institutional governance conversations.

items.title: A mixed-methods analysis of AI scaffolding patterns and student inquiry profiles in a middle-school agriculture-STEM classroom
items.description: Empirical scaffolding data that connects to Femke's existing Zettel notes on scaffolding theory (Tawnya Means, Designed to Fade) — bridges the theoretical debate she's been tracking to actual classroom observations.

items.title: Exploring Teachers' Motivation for Sustainable Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in L2 Education: A Descriptive Qualitative Inquiry
items.description: Qualitative study on what sustains teacher AI adoption over time — provides interview-level evidence for Femke's staff engagement strategy, complementing the TPACK/growth-mindset quantitative findings above.
